examples.en: We learned how to calculate powers in math class.
Powers of 3 get large very quickly.

examples.ko: 거듭제곱 기호는 어깨 위에 작게 써요.
examples.en: You write the exponent small, at the upper right.
How do you enter a power on the calculator?
Shall we write the powers of 2 in order?
Power problems are easy once you find the pattern.

explain: '2의 5제곱'처럼 '~의 ~제곱'으로 읽어요. '제곱', '세제곱'은 곱하는 횟수가 정해진 말이고, '거듭제곱'은 그것을 모두 묶어 부르는 수학 용어라서 주로 수업이나 문제집에서 만나요.
explain_en: You read it as '2의 5제곱' (2 to the 5th power). '제곱' and '세제곱' name a fixed number of multiplications, while '거듭제곱' is the umbrella math term, so you mostly meet it in classes and workbooks.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 무거운 짐도 거뜬히 견디는 튼튼한 소재예요.
examples.en: This bag is made of a sturdy material that easily holds heavy loads.

examples.ko: 이 정도 업무량은 신입 사원도 거뜬히 소화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a new employee can handle this much work with ease.
My cold cleared up easily in just one day.
That athlete lifts even 100 kilograms without difficulty.

examples.ko: 시험 범위가 많아도 이틀이면 거뜬히 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if the exam covers a lot, I can finish it easily in two days.

examples.ko: 할머니는 여든이 넘으셨는데도 산을 거뜬히 오르세요.
examples.en: My grandmother is over eighty, but she climbs mountains with ease.

explain: 힘들 것 같은 일을 쉽게 해내거나 몸이 가뿐하게 나을 때 써요. '들다, 이기다, 나아지다' 같은 동사와 함께 쓸 수 있고, 형용사는 '거뜬하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when something that looks hard is done easily, or when the body recovers lightly. It goes with verbs like 들다, 이기다 and 나아지다, and the adjective form is '거뜬하다'.

examples.en: Please empty the sink strainer every day.

examples.ko: 거름망이 막혀서 물이 잘 안 내려가요.
examples.en: The strainer is clogged, so the water doesn't drain well.

examples.ko: 차를 우릴 때 거름망에 찻잎을 넣어요.
examples.en: When I steep tea, I put the tea leaves in a strainer.
I bought a new strainer at the mart.

examples.ko: 음식물 찌꺼기는 거름망에 모이니까 자주 버려요.
examples.en: Food scraps collect in the strainer, so I throw them out often.
If you strain the broth through a sieve, it is clearer.

explain: 주방 싱크대나 차, 국물을 거를 때 쓰는 도구를 말해요. 체나 '채망'이라고 부르는 사람도 있지만, 싱크대 배수구에 끼우는 것은 보통 '거름망'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the tool used at the kitchen sink or for straining tea and broth. Some people say '체' or '채망', but the one that sits in a sink drain is usually called '거름망'.

examples.en: That team finally grabbed the championship.
He worked for a long time to seize power.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손을 꼭 거머쥐고 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: The child gripped her mom's hand tightly and wouldn't let go.

examples.ko: 신인 배우가 주연상을 거머쥐어서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The rookie actor won the lead acting award and became the talk of the town.
If you want to seize an opportunity, you have to prepare in advance.

examples.ko: 시장의 주도권을 거머쥔 회사가 가격을 정해요.
examples.en: The company that holds control of the market sets the prices.

explain: 손으로 꽉 잡는다는 느낌에서 '우승, 권력, 기회'처럼 큰 것을 차지한다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '잡다'나 '차지하다'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of gripping hard with the hand, and is used for winning big things such as a title, power or a chance. You see it in news articles, while in daily talk people may say '잡다' or '차지하다'.

examples.ko: 이 자리에서 특정 회사를 거명하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to name a specific company here.
The host called out the winners one by one.
The person named in the article apologized right away.
If you mention that name, the mood gets awkward.

examples.ko: 도와준 분들을 모두 거명할 수는 없지만 감사해요.
examples.en: I can't name everyone who helped, but thank you all.
The staff were happy because I praised them by name.

explain: 사람이나 단체의 이름을 직접 말한다는 뜻이라 공식적인 자리, 기사, 연설에서 잘 어울려요. 친구끼리는 '이름을 말하다'라고 해도 돼요. '이름을 거명하다'보다 '~을/를 거명하다'로 쓰는 것이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means saying a person's or group's name outright, so it fits formal settings, articles and speeches. Among friends you can just say '이름을 말하다'. It is more natural as '~을/를 거명하다' than '이름을 거명하다'.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 오래된 거목이 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old giant tree stands at the entrance of the village.
He is a giant of the Korean literary world.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 길가의 거목 한 그루가 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, a huge roadside tree fell.
I rested for a moment in the shade of the big tree.
They say this giant tree has lived for hundreds of years.
That politician is called a giant of the party.

explain: '큰 나무'는 일상 말이고, 거목은 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. 비유로는 한 분야를 오래 이끌어 존경받는 원로에게 '문학계의 거목', '정계의 거목'이라고 해요. '거장'이 뛰어난 솜씨에 초점이 있다면, 거목은 영향력과 연륜이 큰 사람에 가까워요.
explain_en: '큰 나무' is the everyday phrase, while 거목 appears more in writing and news. Figuratively, a respected elder who led a field for many years is called a '문학계의 거목' or '정계의 거목'. Where '거장' focuses on outstanding skill, 거목 leans toward great influence and long standing.

examples.en: The banana peel has turned dark.
Your face has tanned darkish in the sun.
The sky turned dark and then it rained.
The area around my lips looked dark, so I went to the hospital.
The edges of the baked bread are darkish.
Dark clouds are rolling in.

explain: 완전히 검은 것이 아니라 '조금 검은' 정도일 때 써요. '검다'보다 약하고, 색이 변했거나 탔을 때 자주 어울려요. 같은 뜻의 '거무스레하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes something not fully black but somewhat dark, weaker than '검다'. It suits things whose color has changed or tanned. There is also a near-identical form, '거무스레하다'.

examples.en: Maybe you were tired, but your face looks dull and dark.
My dull, dark skin is a worry.
The old wall has turned a dingy dark color.
I left the peeled apple out and it turned dingy dark.
The bottom of the pot is dingy and dark from the smoke.
I always put on sunscreen so my skin doesn't get dark and dull.

explain: 검은색인데 깨끗하지 않고 칙칙해 보일 때 써요. '거무스름하다'보다 느낌이 좋지 않아서 사람 피부에 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It describes a dark color that looks dull or unclean. Its feel is more negative than '거무스름하다', so it can be rude when used about a person's skin.

examples.ko: 며칠 면도를 안 했더니 턱이 거뭇거뭇해요.
examples.en: I haven't shaved for a few days, so my chin is shadowed with stubble.
Dark spots have appeared on the banana.
My son's upper lip has started to get a dark shadow.
The wall got stained with dark patches of mold.

examples.ko: 감자 껍질이 거뭇거뭇해서 다 깎아 냈어요.
examples.en: The potato skin had dark spots, so I peeled it all off.
The sky grew dark in patches and then a shower poured down.

explain: 여기저기 검은 것이 조금씩 보이거나 군데군데 어둡게 보일 때 써요. 수염이 막 자랄 때나 과일에 점이 생길 때 잘 어울려요. 전체가 고르게 어두운 '거무스름하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when dark bits show up here and there, or patches look dim. It suits fresh stubble or spots on fruit. It differs from '거무스름하다', which describes an even darkness overall.

examples.en: The soldier saluted the general.

examples.ko: 아이가 경찰관 아저씨께 거수경례를 하며 인사했어요.
examples.en: The child greeted the police officer with a salute.
Your saluting posture looks really cool.
At the graduation, the juniors sent off their senior with a salute.

examples.ko: 거수경례는 오른손을 이마 근처에 올려서 해요.
examples.en: For a salute, you raise your right hand near your forehead.

examples.ko: 주인공이 마지막에 거수경례를 하는 장면이 인상 깊어요.
examples.en: The scene where the hero salutes at the end is memorable.

explain: 군인이나 경찰이 오른손을 들어 하는 경례를 말해요. '거수경례를 하다'로 쓰고, 손을 들어 장난스럽게 인사할 때도 이 말을 가져다 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the salute that soldiers and police give by raising the right hand. It is used as '거수경례를 하다', and people sometimes borrow it for a playful hand-raised greeting.

examples.en: Your eyes look half-closed, maybe because you're sleepy.
He looked at me with bleary, half-shut eyes.
After staying up all night, my eyes have gone bleary.
He opened his eyes drowsily and got up.

examples.ko: 약을 먹고 나서 눈이 거슴츠레하고 졸려요.
examples.en: After taking the medicine, my eyes are heavy and I feel sleepy.

examples.ko: 눈이 거슴츠레해 보이는데 어제 못 잤어요?
examples.en: Your eyes look bleary. Didn't you sleep last night?

explain: 졸리거나 피곤하거나 취해서 눈이 반쯤 감긴 듯 흐릿할 때 쓰는 말이라 '눈'과 함께 가장 많이 써요. '졸리다'처럼 상태를 말하는 것이 아니라 눈 모양과 느낌을 그리는 표현이에요.
explain_en: It is used when the eyes look half-shut and hazy from sleepiness, tiredness or drunkenness, so it pairs mostly with '눈'. Unlike '졸리다', which names a state, it paints how the eyes look.

examples.ko: 거식증은 마음의 병이기도 해서 치료가 필요해요.
examples.en: Anorexia is also a mental illness, so treatment is necessary.
My friend goes to the hospital because of anorexia.

examples.ko: 거식증에 걸리면 음식을 거의 먹지 못해요.
examples.en: If you have anorexia, you can hardly eat anything.

examples.ko: 거식증 환자를 가족이 옆에서 도와줘야 해요.
examples.en: Family should support people with anorexia from beside them.

examples.ko: 다이어트가 지나치면 거식증으로 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Excessive dieting can lead to anorexia.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 청소년 거식증이 늘고 있다고 해요.
examples.en: The news says teenage anorexia is increasing.

explain: 먹는 것을 두려워하거나 거부하는 병을 뜻하는 의학 용어예요. 반대로 폭식을 반복하는 병은 '폭식증'이라고 해요. 뉴스나 건강 이야기에서 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a medical term for an illness in which a person fears or refuses food. The opposite pattern of repeated binge eating is called '폭식증'. You can meet it in news and health topics.

examples.ko: 이번 실수를 거울삼아 다음에는 더 조심할게요.
examples.en: I'll learn from this mistake and be more careful next time.
Take your senior's experience as a lesson.
People who learn from failure end up succeeding.
You should learn from the past and prepare for the future.

examples.ko: 회사는 그 사고를 거울삼아서 안전 규칙을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The company took that accident as a lesson and changed its safety rules.

examples.ko: 남의 잘못도 거울삼으면 많이 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you learn even from others' mistakes, you can gain a lot.

explain: '~을/를 거울삼아'의 꼴로 가장 많이 쓰고, 지난 일이나 남의 일에서 교훈을 얻는다는 뜻이에요. '교훈으로 삼다'와 비슷하지만 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is most often used in the form '~을/를 거울삼아', meaning to draw a lesson from past events or others' experiences. It is close to '교훈으로 삼다' but sounds a bit more written.

examples.en: The skin of the apple got scratched.
Don't judge people just by their outside.

examples.ko: 이 책은 거죽이 낡았지만 내용은 좋아요.
examples.en: This book's cover is worn, but the content is good.

examples.ko: 수박 거죽을 두드려 보면 익었는지 알아요.
examples.en: If you knock on the surface of a watermelon, you can tell if it's ripe.
The sofa covering tore, so I put on a new one.
The outside is fine, but the inside is all rotten.

explain: '겉'과 비슷하지만 속과 대비해서 겉모습이나 겉껍질을 말할 때 자주 써요. 반의어는 '속'이에요. '겉'보다 말투가 조금 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to '겉' but is often used when contrasting the outside with the inside. Its opposite is '속'. It can sound a little rougher than '겉'.

examples.en: I got rained on and look like a total wreck.
After working all night, I came home looking a mess.
Where are you going looking like that?

examples.ko: 머리도 안 빗고 거지꼴 그대로 나왔어요.
examples.en: He came out looking a mess, without even combing his hair.
After the hike, everyone looked like a mess.
Even though he looked shabby, his expression was bright.

explain: 옷이나 모습이 너무 지저분하고 초라할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '거지꼴이 되다', '거지꼴로 다니다'처럼 써요. 남에게 직접 말하면 무례하니 자기 모습이나 친한 사이에서만 쓰세요.
explain_en: It is a casual word for looking very untidy and shabby, typically in '거지꼴이 되다' or '거지꼴로 다니다'. It is rude to say directly to someone, so use it about yourself or with close friends.

examples.ko: 차를 정비 업체에 맡기고 나서 소음이 거짓말처럼 사라졌어요.
examples.en: After I left the car with a repair shop, the noise vanished as if by magic.
After I took the medicine, my headache disappeared like magic.
Unbelievably, the sky cleared up.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 막히던 문제가 거짓말처럼 풀렸어요.
examples.en: The problem I was stuck on the day before the exam got solved just like that.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 거짓말처럼 하루아침에 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: That shop shut down overnight, as if it were unreal.
It may sound like a lie, but it's all true.

explain: 믿기 어려울 만큼 갑자기, 완전히 변하거나 사라질 때 써요. 뒤에는 '사라지다, 낫다, 풀리다' 같은 말이 잘 어울려요. 좋은 일이든 나쁜 일이든 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when something changes or disappears so suddenly and completely that it is hard to believe. It goes well with verbs like 사라지다, 낫다 and 풀리다, and works for good or bad events.

examples.en: The long skirt was cumbersome, so I changed into pants.
If you have a lot of luggage, travel becomes a hassle.
Please leave out the bulky packaging.
The gloves are so thick that they feel cumbersome.
If your clothes are cumbersome, it's hard to exercise.
I got a gift, but honestly it was a bit of a burden.

explain: 물건이나 일이 크거나 많아서 움직이기 불편하고 방해될 때 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '거추장스러워요', '거추장스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 사람에게 쓰면 '짐이 되는 존재'처럼 들려서 아주 거칠어요.
explain_en: Use it when something is bulky or excessive and gets in the way of moving or doing things. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, giving '거추장스러워요' and '거추장스러운'. Said about a person it sounds like calling them a burden, which is very harsh.

examples.en: The coach's future hasn't been decided yet.
I hear the president will soon announce his own future plans.
The team atmosphere is unsettled over the question of who stays or goes.
There is a lot of talk about the minister's fate.

examples.ko: 앞으로 거취를 어떻게 할지 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm thinking about what to do next in my career.

examples.ko: 그는 거취에 대해 말을 아끼고 있어요.
examples.en: He is holding back about his next move.

explain: 어디에 머물지, 자리에 남을지 떠날지 같은 앞으로의 진로와 입장을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '거취를 표명하다', '거취가 주목되다'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '앞으로 어떻게 할 거야?'처럼 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to where someone will go or whether they will stay or leave, meaning their future course or position. In news you see '거취를 표명하다' and '거취가 주목되다'. In daily talk people spell it out, like '앞으로 어떻게 할 거야?'.

examples.en: My bag kept getting in the way, so I put it on the floor.
My long hair gets in the way.
Please clear away anything that is in the way.

examples.ko: 좁은 부엌에서 서로 거치적거리지 않게 조심해요.
examples.en: In the narrow kitchen, we are careful not to get in each other's way.
The pants were long and got in my way when I walked.
I moved the bags to one side in case they got in the way.

explain: 몸이나 물건이 걸려서 움직임이 불편하거나 일에 방해가 될 때 써요. 비슷한 '방해되다'보다 몸에 걸리는 느낌이 강해요. 사람에게 쓰면 '걸리적거리다'와 마찬가지로 '귀찮게 방해한다'는 거친 느낌이 돼요.
explain_en: Use it when something catches on your body or hinders movement or work. It feels more physical, like snagging, than the similar '방해되다'. About a person it sounds harsh, as if they are annoyingly in the way.
